prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1270; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss was received for a low-speed head-on collision involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports neck pain and was transported from the scene, and the claim has been assigned for review.

Entry 2: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver listed on the policy is the person who reported the loss, and the policy was in force on the date of loss.

Entry 3: Photographs taken at the scene show the front-end damage on both vehicles, and the damage pattern is consistent with the described impact. No independent witnesses have been identified, so the photos are the main independent record of the collision.

Entry 4: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact is now routed through the attorney's office. A recorded statement was requested and the claimant's account has been consistent across each conversation to date.

Entry 5: Medical records were received showing a diagnosis of whiplash, which fits the mechanism and force of a collision of this type. No prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the records reviewed.

Entry 6: Vehicle records show no earlier damage to the front end, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start. Repair estimate has been reviewed and the scope of work matches the impact described.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and has tapered as the claimant's symptoms improved. File remains open pending receipt of the final treatment summary and the attorney's demand package.
